Anthropic's proposed stock market listing could become one of the biggest investment events of 2026. The company behind the Claude artificial intelligence platform is targeting a valuation of around US$1 trillion, potentially rising to US$1.4 trillion on a fully diluted basis. That would make it one of the largest technology IPOs in history. [...] According to Anthropic's IPO disclosures, its annualised revenue run rate reached approximately US$81 billion by the end of October. That is extraordinary growth for a company only five years old.

However, revenue growth alone does not determine whether a trillion-dollar valuation is justified.

The enormous cost of building AI

Developing and operating advanced AI models requires enormous computing power, specialist semiconductor chips, data centres and electricity. [...] Two recent research papers from FactSet provide an interesting perspective on the potential market implications of the listing.

items.title: 🐜 The Trillion-Dollar Ant: Anthropic Prepares for an IPO. Can Claude Justify Such a Valuation?
items.snippet:
💡For investors, it’s important to distinguish between two things:

A company’s v...
items.raw_snippet:
💡For investors, it’s important to distinguish between two things:

A company’s valuation — how much the market is potentially willing to pay for it.

Real economic value — the extent to which the business is capable of sustaining growth, generating profits, and creating cash flow over the long term.

High revenue alone does not guarantee high profitability. AI development requires significant computing resources, infrastructure, investments in equipment, and the recruitment of specialists. [...] What competitive advantages will Anthropic be able to maintain❓

Are overly optimistic expectations already factored into the initial share price❓❓

You should also consider the terms for participating in the IPO through a specific broker, the availability of shares, commissions, and any potential restrictions.

🔋Instead of a conclusion: Artificial intelligence is a business, not just a technology [...] Anthropic’s history shows just how quickly artificial intelligence is evolving into a standalone economic industry.

Just a few years ago, AI developers were viewed primarily as technology startups. Today, they are valued on par with the world’s largest business players.

But investing isn’t a competition to buy the most high-profile stories.

Even a promising company may turn out to be too expensive to buy at its current valuation.
